core_classification.analysis: Widdowson directly avows a loving emotional state, making T dominant. In this courtship setting, the declaration also helps invoke a serious relational undertaking and supports his request for a chance to win Monica, giving P moderate support. His choking and the emotional solemnity of this first declaration indicate intensity but do not show that the words are a reflex-like expressive discharge, so E receives no support.
core_classification.ambiguity: The main uncertainty is how much undertaking force belongs to the core declaration itself rather than to the adjacent promises and courtship requests.

utterance_status.description: Widdowson directly says “I love you with all my soul” to Monica during their courtship conversation.

contextual_interpretation: The declaration follows Monica’s conditional willingness to continue seeing Widdowson while remaining free. It is his first explicit avowal, delivered solemnly and with visible emotion, and it forms part of an effort to continue the courtship under her rules. Monica does not reciprocate the declaration; she instead negotiates boundaries, which Widdowson promises to respect. This framing supports both sincere-seeming avowal and some relational commitment, without establishing expressive/reflexive force.

evidence.quotation_or_description: “I love you with all my soul”
evidence.supports: A direct and emphatic presentation of Widdowson’s loving emotional state, strongly supporting T.

evidence.quotation_or_description: “he choked a little at this first utterance of the solemn word”
evidence.supports: Shows that this is his first explicit declaration and that it is emotionally weighty; choking indicates intense delivery but does not independently establish E.

evidence.quotation_or_description: “and your rules shall be mine. Give me a chance of winning you.”
evidence.supports: Places the declaration within a serious courtship undertaking and supplies moderate support for P, while also showing that much of the explicit commitment lies in adjacent language.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Monica insists that she “must still be perfectly free,” and Widdowson answers, “Perfectly!”
evidence.supports: Confirms that the declaration occurs amid negotiation of relational terms rather than constituting an accepted engagement or reciprocal commitment.

ontology_assessment.diagnosis: T captures the direct avowal, while P captures its limited undertaking force in courtship. Emotional delivery can be recorded contextually without E, and no important aspect of the core force falls outside T/P/E.
